title: Magnetar Retail POC: Costing, Benchmarks & Runway
next_steps: Redwood to share detailed per-token cost model and quantization options by 2027-10-25
Customer to send sample request distribution and 1K representative prompts by 2027-10-24
Schedule 90-min benchmark run week of 2027-10-31 (Jordan/Lee to run)
action_items: Owner: Lee Chen; Item: Build a micro-benchmark harness with customer sample prompts and include KV cache on/off toggles; Due: 2027-10-25
Owner: Aisha Rahman; Item: Provide 1K anonymized prompt samples + QPS profile; Due: 2027-10-24
Owner: Jordan Patel; Item: Send Redwood security overview + SOC2/ISO artifacts and network design for Private deployment; Due: 2027-10-26
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-21
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Lee Chen (Redwood SE), Maria Torres (Redwood SA), Aisha Rahman (Magnetar Head of ML), Tom Becker (Magnetar CTO), Priya Singh (Platform), Noah Li (SRE), Claire Gomez (Product)
transcript_body:
00:00 Jordan Patel: hey everybody, thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood, we'll focus today on scoping the poc around cost and benchmarks, and make sure the runway works with Magnetar's budget.
00:12 Aisha Rahman: thanks, Jordan, quick context — we run personalization at checkout, so latency is like really important, under 120 ms p95 ideally, and it's a mix of short prompts plus some user-state vectors.
00:28 Jordan Patel: got it, low latency, high QPS during peak, and there's some state that could be cached. We'll talk through per-token estimates, batching and KV prefix cache.
00:40 Lee Chen: hi all, Lee here. a couple clarifying q's up front: what's your expected concurrency and average request size in tokens? that drives a lot of cost math.
00:51 Aisha Rahman: current numbers — baseline is 250 rps during peak, spiking to 1.2k for short promos, average prompt payload is around 24 input tokens, and output is ~40 tokens on avg. We also have a few long-form flows but they're <5% of traffic.
01:10 Tom Becker: and we have a hard monthly budget the execs set, around $18k/mo for the personalization LLM portion for the pilot. so we need to model how that maps to per-token pricing and infra.
01:25 Lee Chen: okay that's helpful. quick back-of-envelope: if you do hosted and assume 8K tokens per second at peak, we need to estimate tokens per minute and multiply by per-token unit. But there are knobs — batching will reduce total tokens billed per request slightly by amortizing overhead, and caching can eliminate repeated prefixes.
01:45 Maria Torres: also worth calling out quantization: 8-bit or 4-bit model variants can reduce GPU costs and increase throughput; we'll include those in the bench. they sometimes slightly affect quality, so we should capture eval passes.
01:58 Priya Singh: one constraint: we must keep all user identifiers encrypted and not leave raw PII on third-party hosted logs; we could do tokenization, or we may prefer Private deployment if logs are non-negotiable.
02:12 Jordan Patel: noted. we'll include both Hosted API and Private deployment options in the economic model; highlight differences in unit cost and operational overhead.
02:22 Claire Gomez: success criteria from product side: p95 latency <120ms, quality retention above current rule-based baseline (we'll share eval prompts), and monthly cost <=$18k for pilot.
02:35 Lee Chen: great — we'll set the POC success metrics: latency SLO, quality A/B improvement >=X% (they'll define), and monthly cost within budget. For the bench we'll expose two knobs: batching window (5–40 ms) and prefix KV cache TTL & hit-rate scenarios (low/medium/high).
02:56 Aisha Rahman: can you explain how batching impacts latency vs cost? we worry about tail latency.
03:02 Lee Chen: sure — batching aggregates concurrent requests into one GPU call; that improves throughput and lowers per-token CPU/GPU cycles, so lowers cost per token. However, it adds queuing delay for requests waiting inside the batch, which increases p95. Redwood has continuous batching with adaptive windows — we can test small windows like 5 ms up to 40 ms to see tradeoffs.
03:28 Noah Li: and how about KV cache — what do you cache exactly?
03:31 Maria Torres: the KV cache stores prefix key/value states for autoregressive decoding so repeated prefixes (like product descriptions or standard system prompts) can skip recomputing early layers. if you have a high hit rate for repeated prefixes, effective compute per request drops a lot. we'll show three hit-rate scenarios: 10%, 40%, 70%.
03:55 Tom Becker: sounds good. on pricing, give us per-token estimates for both hosted and dedicated pools? we might consider Reserved capacity if that lowers unit costs.
04:04 Jordan Patel: yes — we'll provide a model. rough example on today's call: hosted baseline per 1K tokens is $0.80 for the medium-sized open model; with batching and cache you can see effective costs drop to $0.40–0.55 per 1K tokens depending on hit rate. Dedicated reserved capacity can push unit costs down another ~20–30% depending on commit and utilization. these are rough numbers — bench will give us concrete.
04:35 Aisha Rahman: are those numbers accounting for quantization?
04:38 Maria Torres: the draft numbers are for FP16 model. for 8-bit/4-bit variants, compute is more efficient; throughput increases and per-token cost drops — but we need quality checks. we'll include quantized runs in bench matrix.
04:52 Claire Gomez: timeline question: how long to get meaningful bench results?
04:55 Jordan Patel: plan—once we have sample prompts and QPS profile, Lee will spin a micro-benchmark harness in ~2 business days, then run a 90-minute benchmark with multiple configurations (hosted/dedicated, batching windows, cache hit-rates, quantization variants). results in 3 days after the run. overall POC phase 3 weeks if everything aligns.
05:15 Priya Singh: security — if we go hosted, what about logs and retention? we need to ensure PII isn't stored and we have audit logs for inference requests.
05:23 Jordan Patel: Redwood hosted can redact and not persist payload contents; we provide SOC2/ISO docs and KMS integration. For stricter compliance, Private deployment inside your VPC with customer-managed KMS is recommended. We'll attach those artifacts.
05:40 Noah Li: network architecture question — can we do a hybrid: host control plane but inference in our VPC?
05:45 Maria Torres: yes — Redwood Private offers a control plane that orchestrates instances inside customer VPC and gives you full network egress control. There's an ops overhead to set up but it's common for retail enterprise.
05:57 Aisha Rahman: let's talk bench matrix specifics — what configs will be included?
06:01 Lee Chen: proposed matrix:
- Model variants: base FP16, 8-bit, 4-bit quantized
- Deployment modes: Hosted API (single region), Dedicated reserved pool (pilot size), Private (VPC) if requested
- Batching windows: 5 ms, 15 ms, 40 ms
- KV cache hit-rate scenarios: 10%, 40%, 70%
- Throughput points: baseline 250 rps, peak 1.2k rps, spike test to 2k rps for 5 mins
- Metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1K tokens, cost per request
06:38 Tom Becker: good. how will we simulate realistic traffic shape? we have promo spikes that last 10–15 minutes with heavy concurrency.
06:45 Lee Chen: please provide a minute-by-minute QPS timeline for a typical promo and also a 24-hour distribution. that lets us run load schedules that reproduce spikes.
06:55 Aisha Rahman: we'll provide that. one more — do you support autoscale burst for dedicated pools, we might need to exceed reserved capacity during campaigns.
07:03 Jordan Patel: yes Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity that can autoscale with defined cost multipliers; we'll model burst usage separately because it can increase monthly spend during campaigns.
07:15 Priya Singh: what's the expected effect of caching on cost for our short prompts? we have a lot of templated system messages.
07:21 Maria Torres: templated system plus product name prefixes are perfect for cache — if your hit rate hits 40% we often see effective compute cost drop 25–45% depending on sequence length. we'll quantify in bench.
07:35 Claire Gomez: ok, so success criteria recap: p95 latency <120ms, monthly pilot cost <=$18k, quality >= baseline, and runbook for scaling to production. correct?
07:43 Jordan Patel: yes. plus a security sign-off. we'll document the runbook and the rollback policies for canary deploys.
07:51 Tom Becker: for the bench, do we need sample data sanitized or can you ingest telemetry?
07:56 Aisha Rahman: we'll sanitize and anonymize — Priya's team will scrub PII and provide tokens.
08:02 Lee Chen: perfect. action items and who does what — Lee will build the harness, Jordan will send security artifacts, Aisha will send samples and QPS profile. Also, we'll propose a focused bench week and a 1-hour results review.
08:19 Jordan Patel: any other blockers?
08:21 Noah Li: just one — we'd like a cost sensitivity table showing how cost scales with cache hit-rate, batching window, and quantization. can you include that?
08:30 Maria Torres: yes we'll produce sensitivity slices: e.g., cost per 1M tokens at 10/40/70% cache hit and batching windows 5/15/40 ms and model precision variants.
08:46 Claire Gomez: timeline on docs? we need that before EOW.
08:49 Jordan Patel: we'll share the draft cost model and bench plan by Monday 2027-10-25.
08:55 Aisha Rahman: perfect.
09:00 Jordan Patel: wrap up — recap next steps: Redwood shares bench plan + security docs; customer supplies prompts + QPS; set benchmark run for week of 2027-10-31; results review early November; POC finish targeted end of Nov if bench looks good.
09:18 Tom Becker: thanks all.
09:21 Jordan Patel: thanks — we'll follow up in email with attachments and calendar invites. bye.
09:25 (call ends)
notes: Tone: pragmatic, engineering-centric scoping. Emphasis on cost/runway and caching/batching tradeoffs. Customer is retail-focused with strict latency constraints and an $18k/month pilot budget. Redwood to run bench with quantization and cache scenarios. Security artifacts requested.
